tool_input.command:
git add -A && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(mission): key dispatch bindings by mission, exclude aborted delegations from Abandon (DES-076 round 3)

C1 (CRITICAL, verified): two dispatches to the same Worker handle
guaranteed a misattribution -- the single active-mission slot could hold
only one pending dispatch, so a second `dispatch --worker bwk` before the
first spawn silently discarded the first mission's binding. This repo
pins one handle per specialty domain, making the sequence normal, not a
corner case. Fixed by keying pending dispatches per-mission
(internal/mission/active.go's new dispatch-pending store): N pending
dispatches to the same Worker now coexist, resolved FIFO (oldest first)
on a matching spawn.

C2 (CRITICAL): ReadActiveMissionBinding's claim-on-ambiguity default was
dangerous once a shared file also carried dispatch bindings -- a partial
ClearActiveMission failure (or DES-076's own consumeDispatchBinding) could
degrade a dispatch into a sticky, trailer-stamping claim. Closed
structurally: dispatch no longer touches the active-mission/origin pair
at all, so nothing but `ethos mission claim` writes there going forward,
and the claim default is now always correct instead of merely usually
correct.

C3 (MERGE-BLOCKER): dispatchedWorker discarded Load/store-resolution
errors and printed `worker ""` for what was actually the correctly
dispatched worker on a corrupt/deleted contract. The function is gone:
Worker is now recorded directly in the pending-dispatch file at dispatch
time, so matching needs no Load at all. A subsequently unloadable
contract for an already-matched pending dispatch is now handled by
dispatchTierB's own existing Load-and-block gate, identically to an
explicit MISSION_ID naming an unloadable contract -- a deliberate,
documented doctrine revision from round 1.

C7: delegations with verdict=aborted (written only by the
max_delegation_depth and content-hash-gate pre-run refusals) are now
excluded from Abandon's blocking gate unconditionally, independent of
BoundVia or any disclaim -- a depth-refused spawn never ran, so it can
never represent real work, and conflating it with a genuine capture would
mislabel the audit trail. Full rejected-alternatives writeup in
store.go's countBlockingDelegations doc comment.

ClearMissionBindings now also clears the closing mission's own
pending-dispatch entry; `mission release` clears every pending dispatch
in the session.

Falsified against pre-fix code before landing: C1's coexistence test,
C7's exclusion + real depth-refusal end-to-end test, and F6's
ClearActiveMission ordering fix (carried forward, still intact) were all
confirmed red via git stash / targeted reverts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
